newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar stocks edge up on high volume.
newsitem.headline: Qatar stocks edge up on high volume.

text.p: Trade at Qatar's official stock exchange rose four-fold in the week to Thursday but the index inched up only marginally, dealers said.
"Trade volume at the official Doha Securities Market rose 433 percent to 90,852 shares compared with 17,031 shares in the previous week," a DSM statement said.
The Commercial Bank of Qatar's 17-share index move up 1.09 point to 142.93 from 141.84 in the previous week.
The value of shares traded amounted to 18.93 million riyals ($5.2 million) against 4.19 million riyals in the previous week - a jump of 351 percent.
"But the dramatic rise in volume and value was not explicitly reflected on the index as the prices of two blue chips suffered a setback," a dealer said.
The shares of Qatar National Bank and Doha Bank Ltd which account for nearly 40 percent of the total market capitalisation shed nine and 10 riyals to 601 and 320 respectively.
The Commercial Bank of Qatar rose 10 riyals to 360, Qatar Islamic Bank 13.75 riyals to 178.75 and Al Ahli Bank added half a riyal to 290.50.
Qatar Insurance advanced five riyals to 585, Qatar Navigation also gained five riyals to 770 and Qatar Cinema rose 20 riyals to 225. Qatar Cement notched 10 riyals up to 325.

Bank shares remained in heavy demand with 81,558 shares changing hands at a value of 18.23 million riyals. Around 8,184 shares valued at 410,387 riyals were traded in the services sector, 300 shares worth 175,500 in the insurance and 810 shares worth 110,250 riyals in the industrial sector.
